label: Handling
description: How the controls feel: the first thing a player notices about a unit.

terms.label: Strafe
terms.description: Moves in any direction regardless of facing and turns instantly; the twin-stick default.

terms.label: Pivot (tank controls)
terms.description: Turns the hull on the spot, then drives forward or back; can't strafe.

terms.label: Steer
terms.description: Turns only while moving, in arcs; fast on straights, can't turn in place.

terms.label: Drift
terms.description: Keeps momentum and slides through turns; needs room to stop.

terms.label: Forward only
terms.description: Must keep moving forward and turns in wide loops; attacks in passes.

tie_breaks.rule: Start from the default handling of the unit's mobility type. Change it only for one of these reasons. (1) A tiny or small unit on legs (two legs or many) gets strafe; this needs no note, since its size and mobility show it. (2) The source clearly shows the unit can't do what the default needs: if it can't turn on the spot, pivot becomes steer; if it can't stop or hover, strafe becomes forward-only; if it can't stop quickly and only slides through turns, with no hover and no sideways move, strafe becomes drift. (3) In a game where players drive the unit (registry control piloted or both), the source clearly shows it sliding sideways at will, such as a hover tank built to strafe: strafe. For reason (2) or (3), name the reason in mobility.notes. Momentum, tilting to speed up, a heavy feel, or an RTS model turning on the spot never change it on their own; put them in mobility.notes. A mode with its own mobility type follows the same rule from that type.
